neighbours.label: 'well', 'bore', 'hole' in the sense of a drilled water or oil well (borehole, well water, well yields)
fire: The village gets its drinking water from a deep borehole near the school.
Arsenic levels in the well water were far above the safe limit.
Engineers measured the well yields across the whole aquifer.
Drake drilled his famous oil well in Pennsylvania in 1859.
Farmers paid to have a new well drilled before the dry season.
Samples from the bore were sent to the lab for testing.
The water table dropped, and several shallow wells ran dry.
Geologists logged the rock layers found along the borehole.
quiet: The village gets its drinking water from a clean river near the school.
Arsenic levels in the tap water were far above the safe limit.
Engineers measured the rainfall across the whole region.
Drake opened his famous oil refinery in Pennsylvania in 1859.
Farmers paid to have a new barn built before the dry season.
Samples from the lake were sent to the lab for testing.
The summer was hot, and several small streams ran dry.
Geologists logged the rock layers found along the cliff face.
